questions.explanation: The Agent is real and recent: AWS's Well-Architected release notes record it on 10-1-2026 and AWS markets it as the next-gen evolution of Trusted Advisor and the Well-Architected Tool; but it appears on neither the in-scope nor the out-of-scope list of the current exam guide (both checked 2026-10), and the guide still names the AWS Well-Architected Tool. The arbitrar is the guide you download today: previews and announcements are context, never key terms, and Trusted Advisor remains in scope with its 56 free checks.

questions.question: A support engineer is choosing a case severity and reviews the first-response ladder as of Oct 2026. Which statements are correct?
options: The highest severity offered is business-critical system down, not production system down
The row that applies is set by the severity chosen, not by the plan alone
A production system down gets a first response under 1 hour on all three paid plans
A general guidance request gets a first response under 24 hours
A production system that is impaired can wait up to 24 hours for a first response
A Basic Support customer can raise the severity level to open a technical case
questions.explanation: When opening a case you choose the severity, and severity rather than plan alone selects the ladder row; the highest row is business-critical system down, not production system down. As of Oct 2026 the ladder gives a production system down a first response under 1 hour on all three paid plans, a production system impaired under 4 hours, a system impaired under 12 hours and general guidance under 24 hours, with business-critical system down answered under 30 minutes on Business Support+, under 15 minutes on Enterprise and 5 minutes from a Unified Operations Incident Management Engineer. The two traps fail on numbers and on scope: production system impaired is under 4 hours, not 24 (T6 numeric bait), and no severity rescues a Basic Support account, because Basic cannot open technical support cases at all, though it keeps billing and account cases and quota increases around the clock. Windows are first-response targets on which AWS commits to every reasonable effort, never resolution times [source: 12-monitoring-support.md 5.2, 5.3, 6].

questions.question: A team walks the AWS Well-Architected Tool review flow documented as of Oct 2026. Put the steps in the order the flow walks them; one option does not belong to the flow.
options: Answer the questions in each lens applied to the workload
Save a milestone as a point-in-time record of the workload
Open a Support Center case so AWS remediates the findings
Define the workload with its owner, stage, up to 5 Regions and 100 account IDs
Work through the improvement plan for each high-risk issue
Read the high-risk issues and improvement plan the Tool returns
questions.explanation: The documented flow starts by defining the workload with its owner, a Production or Pre-production stage, up to 5 Regions and up to 100 account IDs, then applies lenses with the Framework lens on by default, answers the lens questions, reads the high-risk issues plus the improvement plan, fixes them, and finally saves a milestone as a point-in-time record of the workload. The Support Center option is not part of the flow: the Well-Architected Tool is free and merely advises on your own workload, so remediation stays yours, and a support case belongs to the separate five-step incident triage drill where severity starts the first-response clock. Trusted Advisor shows the same split, since it also advises and never enforces [source: 12-monitoring-support.md 4, 6, 7.2].

questions.question: Match each AWS resource a team reads or watches to what it actually gives you, as of Oct 2026:
prompts: A whitepaper published 24 February 2023 and now labelled historical
AWS's appendix naming 28 technologies and concepts for this exam
AWS experts engaged to work directly on your own workload
Twelve months of public service events needing no sign-in
Open and recent account issues shown for 7 days plus a 90-day log
options: The How AWS Pricing Works whitepaper, a historical reference
Service health, the public view of the AWS Health Dashboard
A vocabulary checklist carrying no indication of weight
AWS Professional Services, an engagement rather than a case channel
Your account health, the signed-in view of the Health Dashboard
questions.explanation: The How AWS Pricing Works whitepaper was published 24 February 2023 and AWS now labels it a historical reference, so date-stamp it rather than quoting it as current. The exam guide's appendix of 28 technologies and concepts carries no indication of their relative weight, which makes it a vocabulary checklist rather than a syllabus ranking. AWS Professional Services and solutions architects are engagement offerings, never case channels: opening a case is the Support Center's job, and letting a partner open cases for you is AWS Partner-Led Support on an eligible plan. Health splits by sign-in requirement: service health is public, needs no sign-in and shows service events that are not specific to an AWS account across the last 12 months, while Your account health needs a sign-in and shows open and recent issues for 7 days, scheduled changes and a 90-day event log [source: 12-monitoring-support.md 2.1, 6; 13-pricing-models.md 1.1; 01-exam-guide-cloud-concepts.md 1.3].
